haiku-low.q1: Keys load at process start-up, before readiness. /healthz returns 503 until all three keys load, then 200. A pod gets no traffic until then.
haiku-low.q2: It retries about 6 seconds total, then logs the error and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready. Old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes plus about 30 seconds jitter, it reads the latest version. A changed valid value is swapped in and logged. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value and retries next cycle.
haiku-low.q4: Only in process memory, in SecretStore. They must never appear in logs, metrics, request headers, or disk. Core dumps are disabled because they would capture key values.
haiku-low.q5: Only orders-api-prod pods (read-only on orders-api/prod/*) and security on-call (sole writer). Engineers have no prod read. CI has no secret access.
haiku-low.q6: Old keys remain in git history and in pre-migration images. They become harmless only when revoked at each provider, which happens last, after all pods use new keys and deny policy blocks old images.
haiku-low.q7: Each provider client asks SecretStore for the current value on every call, reading from memory under a lock. It builds the Authorization header from that value. No store network call is made.
haiku-low.q8: All replicas must report the new version ids for all three names via logs or the secret_version_info metric, with no old image running. Provider dashboards must show zero old-key traffic for an agreed window, at least 10 minutes after the last replacement.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access, then copy new keys into the store, then switch the app to read the store and remove keys from the file in one merge, then revoke old keys at providers last. Creating new keys precedes the merge.
haiku-low.q10: From the dev store path orders-api/dev/*, using the developer's SSO identity orders-api-dev. It holds provider test keys. There is no fallback to committed keys, local key files, or prod.
haiku-low.q11: It retries, then logs an error naming the missing key and the error class, never the value, and exits non-zero. It never starts serving with only some keys.
haiku-low.q12: No. The document says rotation cadence is not decided and no schedule is chosen. The 5-minute refresh is only a read interval, not a rotation policy.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first (all three, with retries) at process start; only after the load completes is the ready flag set and /healthz returns 200 (503 until then). Traffic comes only when ready.
sonnet.q2: It retries (1 attempt + 3 retries, 2s apart, ~6s), then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. With maxUnavailable: 0 the rollout halts, old pods keep serving on their still-valid old keys, so customer impact is none.
sonnet.q3: A timer thread every 5 minutes (+~30s jitter) reads the latest version of each key; if the version id changed and the value is valid, the in-memory entry is swapped under a lock and 'secret rotated' is logged. If the read fails, the last good value is kept, a warning is logged, and it retries next cycle.
sonnet.q4: Held in process memory only, in SecretStore (name -> value, version id, time fetched). Never on disk, in environment variables, in logs, metrics or request-header logging, or in the ticket; core dumps are disabled. Only names and version ids may appear in logs/metrics.
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Write: only security on-call. Engineers (orders-api-dev) have no prod access (dev read only); CI has no secret access.
sonnet.q6: The old values stay in git history (history is not rewritten) and in pre-migration images, so they remain visible and valid. They become harmless only when revoked at the providers (after fleet confirmation and after pre-migration images are blocked by the deny policy).
sonnet.q7: Provider clients (PaymentsClient, EmailClient, GeocodingClient) don't copy the key at construction; on each call they ask SecretStore for the current value (in-memory read under a lock, no network call) and build the Authorization header.
sonnet.q8: Rollout step 9, after all replicas run the new image and at least 10 minutes have passed: each replica reports the new version ids for all three names (start-up/refresh logs and the secret_version_info metric); no replica runs an old image; provider dashboards show traffic on new keys and old-key traffic at zero for an agreed window. A missing metric is not a pass; use logs.
sonnet.q9: Create store layout/KMS/access (step 2); write dev/staging test values (3); create new prod keys at providers and write them to the store (4, after code is approved); check prod read access (5); merge code change that switches the app to the store, removes keys from the file and adds the CI guard (6); canary and roll the pods (7-8); confirm (9); block old images then revoke old keys at providers (10). Removing keys from the committed file happens at the code merge, not before the store is populated and verified.
sonnet.q10: From the store's orders-api/dev/* paths (provider test keys written in rollout step 3), using the developer's SSO identity orders-api-dev. No prod access; no fallback to committed keys, a local file, or prod.
sonnet.q11: A missing key counts as a failed read; after the retries (1 + 3, 2s apart) the process logs an error with the name and error class (no value) and exits non-zero. It never starts serving with only some keys.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. The rotation cadence is undecided; the 5-minute refresh is only a read interval, not a rotation policy.
